blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a condition that affects your lungs and causes coughing and shortness of breath.
There is no cure, but treatments can help.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) include:

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: shortness of breath during or after activities you used to do easily, such as walking uphill

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: a cough that does not go away and has mucus (phlegm)

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: frequent chest infections

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: The symptoms of COPD usually start gradually and get worse over time.
For example, when COPD reaches an advanced stage, you may find you're short of breath all the time.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > COPD flare-ups
s: You may have times when your symptoms get worse.
These are known as COPD flare-ups.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > COPD flare-ups
s: Flare-ups can be triggered by:

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > COPD flare-ups
s: chest infections

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > COPD flare-ups
s: breathing in smoke

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > COPD flare-ups
s: breathing in a strong smell from things like cleaning products, hairspray or perfume

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Symptoms of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > COPD flare-ups
s: very hot, cold or windy weather, high pollen or high humidity

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Causes of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is caused by damage to your airways and lungs.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Causes of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: This can include inflammation of your main breathing tubes (chronic bronchitis) or damage to tiny air sacs inside your lungs (emphysema).

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Causes of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: You may be more likely to get COPD if you:

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Causes of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: smoke, or have smoked in the past

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Causes of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: have a job where you might breathe in dust, fumes, chemicals, or other types of pollution

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Causes of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: had a lung condition as a child, such as asthma, or regularly breathed in other people’s cigarette smoke

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help
s: It's important to get medical help if you think you have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you're getting out of breath doing things that never used to take much effort

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you've been coughing for 3 weeks or more

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you keep getting chest infections

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and you're more short of breath than usual

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you're coughing up blood

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you have pain or swelling in 1 of your legs

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you have heart palpitations – this may feel like your heart is racing, going too slowly or skipping a beat, or like a fluttering feeling in your chest

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: You can call 111 or get help from 111 online.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: you have severe difficulty breathing – you’re gasping, choking or not able to get words out

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: your chest feels tight or heavy

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: you have pain that spreads to your arms, back, neck and jaw

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: your lips or skin are turning very pale, blue or grey – on brown or black skin, this may be easier to see on the palms of the hands

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: you feel suddenly confused – for example, you do not know where you are

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Do not drive yourself to A&E. Ask someone to drive you or call 999 and ask for an ambulance.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Bring any medicines you take with you.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Tests for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: If a GP thinks you may have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), they will ask if you smoke and what sort of job you have.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Tests for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: You may need tests, including:

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Tests for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: spirometry tests (a type of breathing test) to check how much air you breathe out

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Tests for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: a chest X-ray

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Tests for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: blood tests

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Tests for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: These tests are used to see how well your lungs are working and to check for any problems.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: There is no cure for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but there are treatments.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Medicines
s: It’s likely you’ll be offered different medicines to help with symptoms of COPD.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Medicines
s: These could include:

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Medicines
s: tablets or a liquid you swallow to make your mucus thinner, so it’s easier to cough up

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Medicines
s: inhalers that contain medicines to help widen your airways (bronchodilators)

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Medicines
s: inhalers that contain steroids you can use during a COPD flare-up

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Medicines
s: If your symptoms do not improve after trying these treatments, you may be offered medicines that you inject, called biologics.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Medicines
s: Your doctor may give you some antibiotics and steroids to keep at home to use if you have a chest infection.
This is called a rescue pack.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Airway clearance devices
s: Your care team may offer you an airway clearance device.
This is a small handheld device you breathe into.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Airway clearance devices
s: It can help keep your airways open and clear the mucus out of them.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Home oxygen therapy
s: You may be offered home oxygen therapy if other treatments do not help.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Home oxygen therapy
s: Home oxygen therapy involves breathing in air that contains more oxygen than normal through a mask or tube connected to a device in your home.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Nebuliser
s: A nebuliser is a machine that delivers COPD medicines as a fine mist, so they can reach your lungs faster.
You may be treated with a nebuliser if you're admitted to a hospital.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Nebuliser
s: Nebulisers are available to buy, but there is no evidence they work better than inhalers for most people with COPD.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Surgery
s: Rarely, you may be offered surgery to help treat COPD if your symptoms are very bad, or other treatments are not helping.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Treatments for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Surgery
s: Surgery usually involves removing damaged areas of your lungs so the undamaged parts can work better.

s: Treatments and medicines for COPD (Asthma + Lung UK)

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Managing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: Making lifestyle changes can help you manage chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Managing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Do quit smoking if you smoke – it's the main thing you can do to improve COPD try to increase your activity levels with regular, gentle exercise, such as walking, cycling, yoga and tai chi keep a diary of things that can cause flare-ups – this can help you avoid triggers have your flu and COVID vaccinations Pulmonary rehabilitation
s: Your doctor may also offer to refer you for pulmonary rehabilitation.
This is usually a 6- to 8-week course where you learn about how COPD affects your body and how exercises can help with symptoms.

s: Keeping active with a lung condition (Asthma + Lung UK)

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Managing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Find out more
s: Pulmonary rehabilitation (Asthma + Lung UK)

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Help and support for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) can affect you physically and mentally.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Help and support for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: Tell your doctor if you think living with COPD is affecting your mental health as they can help.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Help and support for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: You may also find it helpful to get support from other people with COPD.
This could be done in person, or online if you prefer.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Help and support for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
s: There are also national charities that can offer support and information about COPD.

blocks.path: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Help and support for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) > Asthma + Lung UK
s: Asthma + Lung UK is a charity for people who are living with lung conditions.
